why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but cracks are showing. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google is cutting 2027 shipments of a Broadcom-designed AI chip by about a fifth (neither company has commented), and Alphabet sold bonds at wider spreads than in May. After the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders.

Nvidia fell 14% on Friday to US$125.53, its biggest one-day fall since January 2025, after Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining possible accounting issues (no finding of wrongdoing). It is down 22.9% for the week, a seventh straight weekly loss, and 48% below its October record. AMD fell 13%, Micron 14% and Broadcom 12%. Every chip and memory stock in the Nasdaq-100 is now in a bear market. Over the weekend President Trump said he hopes the board rehires Jensen Huang; US futures pointed to a rebound on Monday in Asia (Nasdaq futures +3%).

A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is still priced above 90%, but bets on a bigger 50 bp move were pared back on Friday as markets fell. Governor Cook says policy is not tight enough, while Treasury Secretary Bessent warned more tightening could be a mistake. New York Fed President Williams speaks at 8am Tuesday Melbourne time, and October PCE inflation lands at 12:30am Thursday.

Oracle’s default protection rose to about 328 bp on Friday, a one-month high and above the 300 bp bursting threshold. CoreWeave’s rose as much as 76 bp to about 1,233 bp, below its 1,268 bp record of 5 Nov, while its shares fell 12% (−25.6% for the week). ETFs that would bet against CoreWeave, Oracle and Meta debt have been filed with the SEC.

Anthropic fell 8.5% on its second day to US$88.91, only about 7% above its US$83 IPO price after opening at US$111.50 on Thursday. Its debut drained money from other AI stocks rather than reviving them. Nvidia’s US$118bn of customer guarantees, including about US$105bn tied to one OpenAI data-centre campus, is now under the spotlight with the reported SEC inquiry. (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)
Fell 13 bp to 4.92% on Friday as stocks fell 3.7%, and 4.5% over the week: a clear flight to safety. This is one of the bursting signals: yields falling sharply while stocks fall.
WTI closed at US$83.98 and Brent at US$92.57 on Friday, up on Middle East tensions but down for a third straight week. Oil is not easing the inflation pressure behind Fed hikes.
High-yield spread 323 bp on 13 Nov (320 bp on 12 Nov): broad credit is still calm. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

Friday deepened the rout: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% (seventh straight loss, now in a correction), the Nasdaq 5.3% (2026 gain erased), the Dow 1.9% and small caps 2.5%. Gold fell 4.5% to a 14-month low and Bitcoin dropped below US$59,000, so even havens are being sold.
